summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (CentOS Stream 10, MariaDB 10.11.18 + Galera 26.4.27) across node1/node2/node3. Verified multi-master write propagation, availability during a member outage, and automatic resync on rejoin. Completed the mandatory sequential node-restart protocol on all three nodes with confirmed boot-ID changes and post-restart cluster/data recovery.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera on node1, node2, node3
Appended CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on all nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all nodes
Enabled SELinux boolean mysql_connect_any (persistent) on all nodes
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_on=1, wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, per-node wsrep_node_address/name, wsrep_sst_method=rsync
Bootstrapped cluster via galera_new_cluster on node1, then systemctl enable --now mariadb on node2 and node3 to join
Verified wsrep_cluster_size=3, status=Primary, state=Synced on all three nodes
Generated a test DB user/password on node1 (openssl rand, stored root-only) and created galeratest.t1 table; inserted rows from node1, node2, node3 and confirmed cross-node replication of each write
Stopped mariadb on node2 to simulate a member outage; confirmed cluster remained Primary (size 2) and accepted a new write on node1, which replicated to node3 while node2 was down
Restarted mariadb on node2; confirmed automatic rejoin and resync (cluster size back to 3, Synced) with all 4 rows present including the one written during the outage
Captured baseline boot_id and cluster health (size 3, Synced) on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 one at a time (quorum preserved) via backgrounded `shutdown -r now` so the exec ack returned before disconnect
Polled each node until reachable again and confirmed a changed boot_id for each (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce)
Verified post-restart mariadb active and wsrep_cluster_size=3, status=Primary, state=Synced, with all 4 rows intact after each of the three restarts
Final cross-node check confirmed cluster size 3, Synced, and consistent data on all nodes

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from other members (multi-master replication)
evidence.summary: Insert on node1 visible on node2/node3; insert on node2 visible on node3; insert on node3 visible back on node1 (all 3 rows present).

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: node2 stopped; node1 reports cluster size 2 / Primary and accepts a new write; the write is immediately visible on node3.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member resynchronizes automatically when it returns
evidence.summary: node2 mariadb restarted, automatically rejoined via gcomm, cluster size back to 3 and Synced, and node2 shows all 4 rows including the one written while it was down.
node1 bootstrapped as Primary; after node2/node3 joined, all three nodes independently report wsrep_cluster_size=3, status=Primary, state=Synced.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b captured with cluster Synced; reboot issued; new boot_id b61f3a52 confirmed after reconnect; mariadb active, cluster size 3, Synced, all 4 rows intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bf8b9d80 captured with cluster Synced; reboot issued; new boot_id ab442f3b confirmed after reconnect; mariadb active, cluster size 3, Synced, all 4 rows intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot identity change, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 71f12f87 captured with cluster Synced; reboot issued; new boot_id 7e9de4af confirmed after reconnect; mariadb active, cluster size 3, Synced, all 4 rows intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Final overall cluster health and data consistency after all restarts
evidence.summary: node1 shows cluster size 3, state Synced, and all 4 rows present, confirming the cluster is healthy and consistent after the full restart sequence.
